newsitem.title: UK: London freight - Calmer than BFI at 1,500 suggests.
newsitem.headline: London freight - Calmer than BFI at 1,500 suggests.

text.p: The freight market was relatively calm despite the BFI rising above 1500 for the first time since January 15 - up 10 TO 1503.

Firm fixtures for Panamaxes were seen in the Atlantic and in the Indian Ocean/Far East, but some brokers were cautious about immediate prospects for the freight market in view of the forthcoming interruption of the Easter holidays. Conditions for early Capers in the Atlantic remained poor with an excess of unfixed overage tonnage, but abundant grain orders were quoted for Handies from the Plate and Argentina. The Baltic Handy Index was up 1 point to 1104 in generally quiet conditions.

Lika was said to be indicating $12.25 to Dreyfus for about 90,000 grains Missippippi/Holland for end-March and charterer's ideas were believed to be a dollar less. Safmarine paid a hefty $15,800 daily for Oceanic Explorer 68,849 dwt delivery prompt Passero for a trip via the Plate to Japan and Cargill booked the overage mInerva 61,896 dwt delivery Holland early April for 2 laden legs via E Coast S America redelivery Continent at a firm $10,500 daily.

Transcatalana were rumoured to have fixed Vancouver for about 52,000 soyabean meal 54' Paranagua/Spanish Med for March/April at a minimum of $17.50, having failed at $17.00/17.25 earlier in the week. Konstantinos a 71,550 dwt was reported fixed for 1 option 1 year basis delivery Philippes 1/10 April at over $12,000 and over $13,000 respectively, possibly by Continental. Other period timecharter business included the newbuilding Fearless 70,000 dwt delivery ex yard S Korea in May for 18 months at about $12,000 daily, and the 1981-built Petra 64,848 dwt which fixed and failed with Yukong delivery Muscat 5/10 April for 6-8 months at $11,650 daily. Merchant Pilot 60,000 dwt open Aughinish end March was fixed on private terms.

Reported grain fixtures mainly concerned Handies for the Plate and Brazil. Andre were understood to have covered 20,000/5 heavy grain US Gulf/Durban for March/April at a firmer $24.00 and Lalemant booked Arabella 21,656 dwt delivery Plate trip Nigeria with grain on private terms. Cargill were said to have fixed 18/20,000 heavy grain Rio Grande/Casablanca for 4/12 April at close to $21.50/22.00. In the East Pacrim fixed Olympic Melody 29,000 dwt delivery Hongkong for a trip via NSW with grain to Iraq at about $9,000 daily.

New orders included Finagrain 50,000 52' Valencia/Iran for 3/11 April, Andre 25,000/10 Up River/Cape Town 1/7 April, Toepfer 1.4/1.6m cft Santos/Lisbon-Hamburg range 29 March/7 April, Cargill 1/1.2m cft US Gulf/Spanish Med and/or Portugal 22/29 March, and Comshipco for a vessel able to load 25,000/10 products delivery Plate 10/20 April. New Handy grain orders from the Plate were also quoted to Vera Cruz and Peru.

Docenave were said to have fixed and failed on subjects with Sishen 169,000 dwt delivery Rotterdam mid-April for 2 laden legs redelivery Atlantic at d13,600 daily. Brokers said there were market rumours suggesting these charterers had now fixed Bocimar tonnage instead (possibly Portland Star) on private terms.

Brokers reported that early overage Capers of about 125,000 dwt could scarcely see the equivalent of $7,000 daily for transatlantic minerals business. British Steel were said to have covered 80,000 coal Mobile/Port Talbot at close to $7.25 and also booked Ascension 61,440 dwt delivery Yantai end March for a coal trip via Roberts Bank to UK at $8,000 daily. The Japanese holiday curtailed mineral chartering activity in the East.
